mechanism_narrative: Four consecutive weeks of WORKPLACES mobility rising toward baseline indicates renewed commuting and in-person work routines, which mechanically increases incidental retail and recreation visits (lunch stops, errands) and should push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -21.6 to -9.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory, indicating decoupling of commuting recovery from retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 points week-on-week, it signals a sharp normalization of public transit use that enables greater access to retail and recreation destinations, producing a near-term rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -16.9 to -14.0 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of a TRANSIT week-on-week jump exceeding 5 points, or RETAIL_REC falls despite such a jump.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of declining RESIDENTIAL time-at-home and rising WORKPLACES attendance jointly indicates households are shifting discretionary time away from home toward external activities, and this combined shift amplifies retail visitation beyond what either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 10.9 to 7.3 while WORKPLACES rose from -21.6 to -9.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is not greater than growth predicted by WORKPLACES or RESIDENTIAL alone, i.e., no interaction effect is observed.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-to-week swings in PARKS mobility (from -14.9 to -27.0 to -17.1) reflect a seasonal/weather-driven outdoor recreation regime; when PARKS rebounds strongly, households substitute outdoor recreation for indoor retail and recreation activity, causing RETAIL_REC to grow more slowly or decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -27.0 to -17.1 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with PARKS rebounds rather than falling or stalling, indicating no substitution effect between parks and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (consistently 22-27% above baseline) signals households are still prioritizing essential trips over discretionary shopping, reflecting lingering caution that suppresses growth in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained elevated between 22.4 and 27.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM remains persistently elevated, indicating no suppression effect from essential-trip prioritization.

mechanism_narrative: The steady week-over-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (10.9 to 7.3) indicates households are spending progressively less time at home, a seasonal behavioral shift that should translate into a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell each week from 10.9 to 7.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week despite continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above the -10 threshold, it indicates a policy-driven reopening milestone (e.g., office capacity restrictions lifted) that triggers a surge of after-work and lunch-hour retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -9.6 in the most recent week, crossing above -10 for the first time
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing above -10, or continues to decline despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sustained increases in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicate a compounding recovery of daily mobility infrastructure usage, where commuters both travel more and work on-site more, jointly producing a larger boost to RETAIL_REC than either factor alone would generate over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -20.7 to -14.0 and WORKPLACES rose from -21.6 to -9.6 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no larger than that predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES individually, indicating the interaction term adds no explanatory power.
